exposure: intrapartum ultrasonographic parameters (fetal occiput position, biometry number, viability, presentation, estimated fetal weight, Levator Hiatus APD at rest and Valsalva, Angle of progression (AOP))
outcome: mode of birth (Intrapartum cesarean section, normal vaginal delivery)
cohort: The study included 609 primiparous term singleton vertex presentation pregnant patients aged >18 years, admitted in the first stage of labor between January 2021 and May 2023.
finding: Maternal age, BMI, gestational age, occiput posterior position, Angle of progression at Valsalva, and levator hiatus anteroposterior diameter at Valsalva were independent significant predictors for intrapartum cesarean section, with specific high ratios of HC/APD at rest, BPD/APD at Valsalva, and HC/APD at Valsalva, coupled with low APD at Valsalva and AoP Valsalva values, indicating a higher likelihood of cesarean section.
mod_finding: Maternal age, BMI, gestational age, occiput posterior position, Angle of progression at Valsalva, and levator hiatus anteroposterior diameter at Valsalva were significant predictors for intrapartum cesarean section, with specific ratios of HC/APD and BPD/APD also being indicative of the mode of delivery.
